- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off behavior or market correction.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; increase downward bias in next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5-7 days) — cap forecast at 1-2% below recent 18-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model often drifts toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 18-day moving average unless sentiment shifts.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 3 days, adjust entire 30d forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to account for lagged market reaction.
